newsitem.title: PERU: Guerrillas suffer more reverses in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas suffer more reverses in Peru.

text.p: Peruvian troops killed three guerrillas in a clash on Sunday in the jungle area of Alto Pacae in the central Huanuco department, the defence ministry said on Monday.

In an earlier clash in the Angashiyacu area, also in Huanuco, a soldier and a guerrilla were killed on Saturday and seven guerrilla suspects taken prisoner, the ministry said in a statement. On Friday eight guerrillas and one soldier were killed in a battle in the highland department of Huancavelica.
The guerrillas are presumed to be members of the Maoist Shining Path movement, which is seeking to reactivate its 16-year-old war after severe setbacks in recent years.

The army's anti-guerrilla operations are currently focused on the central Andes, specifically Huancavelica, Junin and Ayacucho departments, where 2,000 soldiers have since early September been hunting down Shining Path's military leader Oscar Ramirez Durand, alias "Comrade Feliciano."

Ramirez has gradually come to dominate the Shining Path, greatly weakened since the 1992 capture of its leader Abimael Guzman, and has steered the group to a bloodier course this year, according to security force sources.
About 30,000 people have been killed since 1980 in guerrilla wars launched by the Shining Path and the smaller Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
